title: Should Alphabet split into soft-mask handling, indexed starts, key symbols and structural ranks?
body:
`Alphabet` in `libsufr/src/build.rs` has three variants: `Dna { ignore_softmask }`, `Amino` and `Bytes`. The CLI picks `Dna` with `-d` and `Bytes` otherwise. No flag selects `Amino`, and the build treats it exactly like `Bytes`. The build reads the alphabet in two places, and two related settings never consult it:

| Concern | Code | What sets it today |
|---|---|---|
| Rewriting the text | `normalize` | Every variant uppercases lowercase bytes. `Dna { ignore_softmask: true }` writes `N` over them instead. |
| Which suffixes are indexed | `keep_table` | `Dna` keeps suffixes starting with `A`, `C`, `G`, `T` or `$`. The others keep all of them. |
| Ranks in the key | `Packing::from_occupancy` | The distinct bytes the text holds. The alphabet plays no part. |
| Sentinel and delimiter | `SENTINEL_CHARACTER`, `-D` | Byte values. They work only when they sort below every other byte in the text. |

The header stores `is_dna` and `ignore_softmask`. Only `summarize` reads them.

Mixing these concerns causes the following:

- `-i` excludes soft-masked suffixes only because `normalize` writes `N` and `keep_table` then drops suffixes that start with `N`. The clap definition therefore has `requires = "is_dna"`, so the flag cannot apply to protein.
- Under `-i` the file stores `N` in place of the soft-masked bases, and `extract` prints those `N`s.
- `Bytes` still uppercases lowercase, so it does not keep the raw bytes.
- Search never case-folds a query. A lowercase query matches nothing in any mode.
- Key width depends on whichever stray bytes the text happens to hold (sufr-aa4802).
- Rank 0 goes to whichever byte in the text is smallest, which is not always `$` (sufr-b96ee1).

## Proposal

Replace `Alphabet` with three independent settings, and give the structural bytes ranks of their own:

1. Soft-mask handling: `Fold` uppercases lowercase bytes, as the build does today. `Preserve` keeps the bytes as they are. Under `Exclude`, no suffix starts at a soft-masked position and no match runs into one. `Exclude` works for any alphabet. If the build marks the positions in a mask kept beside the text rather than writing `N` over them, `extract` returns the input bases.
2. Indexed starts: either every position, or only the positions whose byte is in a given set (`ACGT` for DNA).
3. Key symbols: either the bytes the text holds, as today, or a declared set such as `ACGTN`. With a declared set, every other byte shares one "other" rank, which is the second option in sufr-aa4802.
4. Structural ranks: the sentinel and the delimiter take the lowest fixed ranks, below every symbol, whatever their byte values. That settles sufr-b96ee1 by construction and lifts the "must sort below" condition on `-D` (`build.rs:67`).

`-d` becomes a preset: `Fold`, starts in `ACGT`, symbols `ACGTN`. `-i` selects `Exclude` and no longer needs `-d`. The header records settings 1 to 3, so search can fold a query the same way the build folded the text.

## Rejected

- Keeping `Alphabet` and fixing sufr-aa4802 and sufr-b96ee1 inside it. Each fix would add one more special case keyed on `Dna`, and `-i` would stay tied to `-d`.

## Cost

- A new `.sufr` format version, 7 to 8, because the header gains fields.
- The 12 fixtures compared by `create_bytes_match_fixtures` in `sufr/tests/cli.rs` need rebuilding.
- `table()` in `libsufr/tests/oracle.rs` needs cases for each combination of settings.
- `Alphabet::Amino` goes away.

## Open

- Settings 1, 2 and 4 look mechanical. Setting 3 under a seed mask needs a rule: bytes that share the "other" rank can tie in the key while differing in the text, and `MaskedKeys::order_ties` assumes that cannot happen. sufr-aa4802 spells this out.
- What `Exclude` should store on disk: a byte reserved for masked positions, or a separate bit array. A query containing `N` matches today's `-i` regions, and nobody has checked whether any caller depends on that.
- Whether `Preserve` or `Fold` should be the default when `-d` is absent.

notes.author: Jeb Rosen/4f1d36b6
notes.text:
Settings 1 and 2 of the proposal replace `Alphabet` in 8851861 on branch `worktree-split-alphabet`, rebased on `dev` at 3b00595 and not yet merged. Settings 3 and 4 are not in it.

- `SoftMask` in `libsufr/src/format.rs`: `Fold` (default), `Preserve`, `Replace(u8)`, set with `SuffixArrayBuilder::with_soft_mask`. It is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so adding an exclude mode later does not break callers.
- `SuffixArrayBuilder::with_starts(&[u8])` indexes only suffixes starting with those bytes, plus the sentinel. The default is every suffix.
- CLI: `--soft-mask fold|preserve|<char>` and `--starts <chars>`. `-d` is short for `--starts ACGT`, `-i` for `--soft-mask N`, and `-i` still requires `-d`.
- Header bytes 1 and 2 hold the soft mask and its replacement byte, and a 32-byte bitmap of the starts follows the seed mask. `Header::soft_mask` and `Header::starts` expose them. The format stays at 7, which no release has written; Jeb ruled out a second bump in this release cycle.

Where it departs from the proposal:

- There is no `Exclude` mode. A DNA build with `Preserve` and `--starts ACGT` keeps the soft-masked bases in the text and indexes no suffix starting in one, so `extract` returns the input bases with no mask stored beside the text. A match runs into a lowercase region only for a lowercase query. Protein gets the same effect from `Preserve` and a `--starts` list of the uppercase residues.
- `Fold` stays the default, so existing invocations build the same suffix array. The 12 fixtures match their earlier copies byte for byte from the text onward.
- Search still does not fold queries. The header now records the soft mask, so it could.

Settings 3 and 4 stay open under sufr-aa4802 and sufr-b96ee1.
